chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they voluntarily surrender of themselves.

key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّهُمْ: They made permissible for themselves / voluntarily surrendered

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's dominion is not inherent but contingent upon the believer's voluntary concession (*tark*) of their spiritual vigilance. This conditional authority underscores the Shia theological emphasis on human agency (*ikhtiyar*), where maintaining righteousness actively nullifies the Shaytan's influence, distinguishing the steadfast believer from those who succumb to his whispers.
